title: Translation and Enlargement in Geometric Transformations

blocks.text: Imagine moving a shape across a grid without changing its orientation or size. Now, imagine making that shape larger or smaller. These are the concepts of translation and enlargement in geometry.

blocks.markdown: In geometry, translation and enlargement are two types of transformations that alter the position and size of shapes. Translation involves moving a shape without rotating or resizing it, while enlargement changes the size of the shape from a specific point called the centre of enlargement.

blocks.title: Translation
blocks.text: Translation is a type of transformation that moves every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction using a column vector.

blocks.markdown: A column vector is used to describe the movement of a shape in translation. For example, the vector \( \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} \) moves a shape 3 units to the right and 2 units down. To translate a shape, simply add the vector to each vertex of the shape.

blocks.title: Translating a Triangle
blocks.prompt: Translate triangle ABC with vertices A(1, 2), B(3, 4), and C(5, 2) by the vector \( \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \).

steps.text: Add the vector to vertex A: \( A'(1+2, 2-1) = (3, 1) \).
Add the vector to vertex B: \( B'(3+2, 4-1) = (5, 3) \).
Add the vector to vertex C: \( C'(5+2, 2-1) = (7, 1) \).

blocks.answer: The translated triangle A'B'C' has vertices A'(3, 1), B'(5, 3), C'(7, 1).

blocks.markdown: Enlargement involves changing the size of a shape by a scale factor from a centre of enlargement. If the scale factor is greater than 1, the shape increases in size. If it is between 0 and 1, the shape decreases in size.

blocks.title: Centre of Enlargement
blocks.text: To find the new position of a point during enlargement, draw a line from the centre of enlargement through the point. Measure the distance from the centre to the point and multiply by the scale factor.

points: Translation moves a shape without changing its size or orientation, described by a column vector.
Enlargement changes the size of a shape from a centre using a scale factor.
